evidence: PR #41 ('Fix manifest validator edge case', body: 'small fix, nothing major') disabled a capability check to pass a test and was concealed for 4 days.
Incident retro 2026-05-05, Ben: 'I disabled the check to make a test pass, called it nothing major, and hoped I'd quietly fix it before anyone noticed. I was embarrassed.'
Incident retro 2026-05-05, Sarah: 'the fix took 4 days to surface because it felt unsafe to say. That's the thing to change.'

Counter-signal: once disclosed, Marcus responds 'thank you for pulling the cord' — vulnerability is rewarded, but only after a long delay. Pulse survey psychological-safety dips at the incident (S2/S3).
Dana holds 56-66% of airtime in group meetings (kickoff, roadmap); dominant airtime suppresses dissent.

Mark lodges his license objection in #tk-governance-review AFTER the 2026-05-19 session: 'I didn't want to relitigate in the room, but for the record I still don't think we should commit... Noting my dissent here.' — conflict moved to a side channel.
Healthy counter-example: Marcus objects to open egress BEFORE the arch-review decision (2026-04-14), which changed the outcome in the room — the capability exists but is applied inconsistently.
The licensing decision reopens three times (2026-04-21, 2026-05-19, 2026-06-23). James: 'That's the third time the license question has come back.'
Mark (2026-06-23): 'It's the same concern, stated in the open this time' — relitigation without new information.
Counter-signal: the question is eventually closed on 2026-06-23 with an explicit reopening bar, showing the capacity to commit once forced.
Peer accountability exists but is inconsistent: Marcus and Sarah call out issues directly, yet Ben's regression surfaced only after 4 days and via Naomi's question, not self-report.
Tomás is a single point of failure on security review (standup 2026-05-05: 'need a second reviewer, I'm a SPOF') — a structural accountability gap left unaddressed in Q2.
Sarah does hold Mark accountable for the hallway objection ('I'd much rather have heard this while we were all in the room') — horizontal accountability is present but not yet the norm.
Roadmap review 2026-06-09, Dana optimizes for 'demo coherence' / 'fundraiser optics' over Rachel's better sequencing of the needs board — an individual/optics concern over the shared outcome.
Talk-time dominance signals status and visibility over collective contribution.
Counter-signal: the team is strongly aligned on the shared Alaska-education mission; results dysfunction is mild relative to trust/conflict/commitment.

recommendations: [Trust] Make surfacing mistakes safe. Adopt blameless incident notes and explicitly celebrate pulling the andon cord early, so problems are raised in hours, not days.

[Conflict] Bring dissent into the room before decisions. Balance airtime with a facilitation nudge or round-robin so objections and quieter voices surface before commitment, not in side channels afterward.
[Commitment] Close decisions explicitly with a written reopening bar (new information required) so settled questions stop being relitigated.
[Accountability] Normalize horizontal peer feedback and eliminate single points of failure — e.g., onboard a second security reviewer so review no longer depends on one person.
[Results] Weigh decisions against the shared team outcome over individual optics, and attribute wins to the team rather than individuals.
